history.content: ok so this is kind of dumb but i need to tell someone. i ran 5k this morning. like actually ran the whole thing without stopping
That’s a real thing to want to tell someone. You ran the whole 5k without stopping, and that matters.

yeah but here's the thing thats making me weird about it. like a year ago i couldnt walk up the stairs at the train station without stopping halfway. my resting heart rate was insane. doctor used the word prediabetic which i still hate. and now i just. ran 5k

That sounds less like one neat feeling and more like a mix of pride, relief, and maybe some old dread getting touched too. I’m curious what it feels like the moment you put those two versions of you side by side?

ok yeah you nailed it actually. its not just happy. when i put them side by side i kind of want to cry?? like proud but also so sad for the version of me that was scared all the time. she really thought that was just how her body was gonna be forever. and i was so ashamed back then i wouldnt even tell people i was struggling

I’m holding both, then, pride and a sad kind of grief for that scared version of you, with shame sitting around the edges. You can leave it there, or we can stay with what that shame was doing back then.

no lets stay with it. the shame thing is the part i havent figured out. i think i was ashamed because i felt like id done it to myself? like i let my body get to that point and everyone could SEE it. my mom would make these little comments. so today running felt like proving something but also i hate that i still need to prove anything you know

That feels like shame mixed with a kind of protest, and maybe some hurt where those comments landed. It sounds like running was both proof and a way of pushing back, in a body that felt visible to everyone.

the hurt one yeah. she still does it. i lost the weight and got fit and last week she goes 'see doesnt it feel better to take care of yourself' like as if i wasnt a whole person before. and the worst part is part of me agreed with her in the moment and i hate that. crossing that finish line this morning i wanted to call her and i dont even know if it was to share it or to win

That sounds like hurt with some shame still hooked into it, and the finish line pulled at both wanting to share and wanting to win. Does it feel more like those two were together, or like one was underneath the other?

underneath i think. like the wanting to win was on top, loud, but if im honest underneath it was just this little kid still wanting her to say im proud of you without the lesson attached. and i didnt call her. i called my sister instead and she just screamed and i cried and that was actually the best part of the whole day
That little kid wanting “I’m proud of you” without the lesson attached lands very clearly. And calling your sister, then crying while she screamed, sounds like the best part found some real company.

yeah. company is the word. honestly i think thats what i actually wanted from the run too, not to prove anything to my mom but to feel like im finally on my own side instead of at war with my body. that probably sounds cheesy but the 5k was kind of me showing up for myself for once
Not cheesy. It sounds like the run was making room for company on your own side, instead of that war with your body.

on my own side. im gonna keep that one. ok i didnt expect to cry into my phone before lunch but i feel weirdly lighter. thank you for not just saying yay good job and actually letting it be the complicated thing it was
I’m glad we could let it stay complicated. It can rest here now, and you can keep “on my own side” if that feels worth keeping.
yeah. letting it rest. thank you, really. ok going to go drink an absurd amount of water and feel my legs being sore in the good way. bye for now
Bye for now. That sore-in-the-good-way sounds nicely earned, and I’ll let it be there with the rest of today.
